title: Console UI: Security → Audit Export configuration page (beta, feature-flagged)
creator: Chloe Martin
links: RBAC + audit log of config changes: ENG-13933
description:
Build the Console UI surface for configuring SIEM-ready Audit Export (beta). This is the customer-facing page under **Security → Audit Export** that lets an admin:

1) Create/manage export destinations (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3)
2) Configure filters (include/exclude rules) with validation and safe defaults
3) View destination health (last delivered, backlog estimate, error states) and basic troubleshooting guidance
4) Send a **test event** to validate connectivity/credentials

All UI must be behind the per-tenant feature flag for the beta. Page should degrade gracefully when backend returns partial health data or when a destination is in degraded/paused state.

Non-goals for beta:
- Full historical backfill UI
- Complex per-field mappings / transformations beyond published schema
- Advanced analytics (that will live in observability dashboards)

Primary users: Workspace/tenant admins; Security/Compliance admins.

Key constraints:
- Must not display secrets (tokens/API keys) after creation; use masked inputs and "rotate" semantics if supported by API.
- UI must clearly communicate **at-least-once** delivery and potential duplicates + recommended dedupe key (link to docs).
- UI must surface RBAC errors with actionable messaging ("You need Security Admin to manage Audit Export").

Entry points:
- Left nav: Security → Audit Export (behind feature flag)
- Deep links from onboarding docs

Design reference: DES-611/612/613.
acceptance_criteria: Feature flag: Page and navigation entry are hidden unless tenant flag is enabled; direct URL access shows "Not available" page (no information leakage).
Destination list page: shows existing destinations with Type, Status (Enabled/Paused/Degraded), Last delivered, Backlog estimate, and Last error (short).
Create destination flow: supports Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3 (beta); form fields match backend schema; includes inline validation and server-side validation error rendering.
Credentials handling: secret fields are write-only; after create/update, UI never renders the original secret value; masked display uses placeholder only.

Filters editor: supports include/exclude rules per spec; shows validation errors from backend (invalid field, invalid regex/pattern, too-broad filter) in a user-readable way; warns about potential volume if filter is empty (default).
Health widget: Destination detail page shows health status, last_success_at, last_attempt_at (if available), error class/message (sanitized), backlog estimate, and a "View troubleshooting" panel.

Test delivery: button to send a test event; shows in-progress state; success shows event_id/request_id and timestamp; failure shows error_id and recommended next action (check token, egress, 429 throttling, etc.).
Error UX: common errors are classified into: Auth, Throttling, Network/TLS, Schema/Validation, Server error; UI copy is reviewed by Security (no sensitive leakage).
Auditability: UI copy links to "Export configuration changes are audited" and (if available in product) deep link to Audit Log search filtered to export config changes.
Tracking/telemetry: emit product analytics events for create/update/delete/test/pause/resume actions (include destination type; no secrets).
Accessibility: form errors are accessible (aria-describedby), status indicators have text equivalents, keyboard navigation works in create flow.
implementation_notes:
UI architecture notes:
- Use existing Console patterns for CRUD resources (List → Detail → Edit drawer/modal).
- Prefer server-side validation as source of truth; client-side validation only for obvious formatting/required fields.
- For error classification, rely on backend error codes where possible (ENG-13929/13928). If error codes are missing, fall back to message pattern matching as interim (document and remove later).
- Health polling: poll destination health every 30s on detail page; list page every 60s; stop polling when tab is not visible.
- Rate limits: avoid aggressive polling across many destinations; cap to N destinations on list view and lazy-load details.
- Sanitization: never render raw connector response bodies; only render sanitized backend-provided fields (error_class, error_message_safe, error_id).

Copy requirements:
- Must say "At-least-once delivery; duplicates possible" near destination enablement and in docs links.
- Provide short "Recommended dedupe key" snippet (request_id + destination_id + event_id) as per schema guidance.

Private deployment considerations:
- Some tenants may not have Datadog endpoint egress; UI should not assume it’s reachable.
- S3 may be S3-compatible in Private; field labels should be neutral ("S3 endpoint" optional, if supported by backend).
rollout_plan:
1) Land UI behind tenant feature flag (ENG-xxxxx flag wiring handled in control plane; Console consumes gate).
2) Enable for internal dogfood tenants only.
3) Enable for 1–2 beta design partners (Solutions Eng-driven) after backend health endpoints stabilize.
4) Expand to remaining beta cohort with SRE monitoring of connector error spikes.

Rollback: disable flag per tenant; UI should cleanly hide without leaving broken nav entries.
testing_plan:
Manual:
- Create/edit/delete each destination type with valid + invalid inputs
- Verify secret fields are never displayed post-save
- Test delivery success + failure flows (401/403, 429, 5xx)
- Validate filters: empty filter, include-only, exclude-only, invalid patterns
- Verify RBAC: user without permission sees appropriate messaging and actions disabled

Automated:
- Component tests for create flow validation rendering
- Playwright E2E for happy path create + test delivery (mock backend)
- Snapshot tests for health states (Enabled/Paused/Degraded + last_error present)

Performance:
- Confirm polling does not exceed expected request rate; validate browser CPU remains reasonable with 20+ destinations.

open_questions: Do we allow multiple destinations per tenant in beta, or cap at 3? UI can support multiple but needs copy/guardrails if backend enforces a limit.
For S3: do we expose SSE-KMS fields in UI for Hosted only, or also for Dedicated/Private (if supported)?
Should "Pause destination" be a UI action in beta, or SRE-only? Backend state machine supports paused; decide per PRD.
What is the canonical docs link target for dedupe guidance (writer wants a stable URL)?
risk_notes:
Main risks:
- Misleading health UI if status semantics change (Enabled vs Degraded vs Paused). Mitigation: use backend-provided status enum and do not infer from metrics.
- Accidental secret exposure in UI logging/analytics. Mitigation: strict allowlist for analytics properties; do not log form values.
- Retry storm / backlog scenarios causing frequent error states. Mitigation: UI should not encourage repeated "Test" clicks; add cooldown and show last test timestamp.
